hook: They are arriving before the food does.
caption:
They are arriving before the food does.

Most North American songbirds time their spring migration to the day, and the day they evolved to arrive is the day the caterpillars hatch in the trees they breed under. Caterpillars are the only food rich enough to feed nestlings to fledging weight in two weeks, and across the continent the warming climate has now pulled caterpillar emergence forward by an average of nine days while the migration itself has only shifted by three. The gap is widening. A 2023 study tracking eighty-six species found that arrivals consistently miss the food peak by a week or more, and chick survival drops accordingly. The flocks you see still come back when their bodies tell them to. The forest they evolved with no longer agrees.
